name: Degree 2, extrema over the two cell ends only (too few points)
source: a variant of Zhang and Shu, J. Comput. Phys. 229 (2010), (2.8)-(2.11), Lemma 2.4, Theorem 2.5 (2.11)

claims.why: avg(p~) = ubar + theta (avg(p) - ubar) = ubar for any scalar theta
the bound holds at the points where the extrema are taken, whatever they are
the average is not a combination of the end values: p = 1/2 - 6y^2 (average 0, both ends -1) lies in [m, M] = [-1, 1/2], but theta = 1/2, so p~ = p/2 != p with no overshoot
